seo.title: Panels, curves and the analyser — OpenMixer
seo.description: How an OpenMixer plugin looks in MOD's pedalboard, what its curves draw, and how to read the analyser: real screenshots, no mock-ups.

hero.title: Panels, curves and the analyser
hero.lede: Each OpenMixer plugin draws its own panel: a pedal in MOD's pedalboard, the same groups on the console and on Zynthian. This page shows what you see and how to read it. Every picture is a screenshot of the real thing. A section whose feature has not shipped yet shows a marked empty frame instead.

docsPanelsCurves.draft: Draft: these MOD pedal screenshots come from the pull request that adds the looks (omx-plugins#71). This page is published when that work merges.

modgui.title: The MOD pedal
modgui.intro: In MOD's pedalboard (mod-ui), each OpenMixer plugin is a pedal. Its face is drawn from the plugin's own description: one framed section per group of controls, each with its name in the corner, and the meters at the bottom.

looks.title: Three looks
looks.text: Every pedal comes in three looks: vintage, a cream face with silver knobs, which is the default; console, the dark face of the OpenMixer console; and 3D, with raised sections. The three small buttons in the pedal's header, V, C and 3D, switch the look while it plays. The pedal keeps its size and its connections; only the drawing changes.

needles.title: Needle meters
needles.text: The METERS section shows needle meters with their scale printed on each face: gain reduction from −60 to 0 dB, input and output level from −60 to +6 dBFS, and the key level from −60 to 0 dBFS. The needles move with the plugin's own meter outputs.

tiers.title: Easy and Advanced
tiers.text: A pedal can show its Easy controls or all of them. Easy keeps what you reach for on every channel: trim, the filters, the gate's threshold and range, each band's frequency and gain, and the compressor's threshold, ratio and makeup. Advanced adds the rest: the gate's attack, release, hold and knee, each band's type and Q, the filter slopes, and the stage order.

matrix.title: The EQ is a row of columns
matrix.text: In the EQ section each band is a column, from low to high: HPF on the left, then bands 1 to 4, then LPF on the right. Each column stacks the same controls in the same order: on/off at the head, then type or slope, frequency, gain and Q. The curve above the columns draws the whole EQ, the HPF and LPF roll-offs included.

curves.title: The curves
curves.intro: A curve shows what a processor does to the sound, drawn from its settings. In the MOD pedal it is marked “modelled”: it is computed from the knobs, not measured from the audio.

eq.title: The EQ curve
eq.text: Frequency runs left to right, from low to high; gain runs up and down, with 0 dB in the middle. Each band bends the line where its frequency is, by its gain, as wide as its Q. The HPF and LPF are drawn as the curve's two ends: the line falls away below the HPF and above the LPF. On the console each band has a dot on the curve that you drag: sideways for frequency, up and down for gain.

comp.title: The compressor's transfer curve
comp.text: The input level runs left to right and the output level bottom to top. Below the threshold the line rises one for one: nothing is changed. Above it the line bends flatter by the ratio, so a louder input comes out less loud; the knee rounds the corner. Turn the threshold, ratio, knee or makeup knob and the curve moves with it.

time.title: Delays and reverbs
time.text: A display of how a delay or a reverb answers over time is not part of any shipped plugin yet. This section waits for it.

console.title: On the console
console.text: Meters ▸ Analyzer shows the live spectrum of the source you choose: frequency left to right, level up and down, with a tilt reference to compare against, the peak readout, and the controls for the trace.

under.title: The spectrum under a curve
under.text: A curve panel can also draw the measured spectrum under its curve, so you see what the EQ is working on. This waits for omx-panel 0.13.8 and its Zynthian side.

zynthian.title: On Zynthian
zynthian.text: Zynthian draws the same groups on its touch screen. Its own pages, with screenshots from the Pi, are in the Zynthian guide.
